literal: Having read, even having understood, and having taught to others, oneself not submitting than the fool fools there are not.
translation: There are no greater fools than the fool who reads, understands, and teaches others, yet fails to control his own conduct.
modern: நூல்களைப் படித்து, அவற்றின் பொருளை உணர்ந்து, மற்றவர்களுக்கும் எடுத்துச் சொல்லியும், தான் அந்த நெறிப்படி நடக்காத முட்டாளை விடப் பெரிய முட்டாள்கள் யாருமில்லை.
explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate form of folly. It describes a person who has read widely, understood the meaning of what they read, and even teaches those principles to others. However, if they fail to apply that knowledge to control their own behavior, their learning is useless. The word 'aṭaṅkā' means not submitting or not controlling oneself, showing that true wisdom requires living by what one knows, and lacking this makes one the greatest fool.
